we propose a broadcast-based distributed algorithm that converges asymptotically to stationary solutions for the (constratined) nonconvex minimization of the agents' sum utility plus a regularizer over time-varyig digraphs, and that the proposed algorithm outperforms the current state of the art.
a novel algorithm for nonconvex distributed constrained optimization over time-varing networks is presented and its convergence to stationary points is proved.

we introduce a novel broadcast algorithmic framework that allows for the distributed optimization of the sum of nonconvex and nonsmooth functions, with no need of double-stochasticity and knowledge of the graph.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design, analysis, and numerical evaluation of distributed algorithms for nonconvex multi-agent optimization over time-varing networks, and it is a step towards a more complete understanding of the capabilities of distributed algorithms for solving nonconvex problems over networks.

the design and analysis of distributed optimization methods for multiagent networks with time-varying communication topologies, and with the application of the proposed methods to a number of problems of interest in signal processing and control.

this paper provides a novel broadcast-based framework for distributed nonconvex optimization over arbitrary time-varying graphs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose the first broadcast-based algorithm for nonconvex distributed multiagent optimization over arbitrary time-varying graphs.

we have developed a novel distributed algorithmic framework that is applicable to both convex and non-convex optimization problems, and is capable to deal with time-varying communication networks, and is able to handle both the cases when the agents have access to their local objective functions or when they only know their gradients.
we provide a distributed algorithm for solving a nonconvex optimization problem over a time-vary network.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed algorithmic framework can be employed to solve a variety of distributed problems in multiagent networks, such as distributed optimization, distributed machine learning, and consensus-based control.

the broadcast-based distributed SCA framework, coupled with a novel tracking mechanism, can be used to efficiently and effectively solve nonconvex distributed constrained optimization problems over arbitrary, timevarying digraphs without the need of the double-stochastic property of the consensus matrices.
broadcast-based methods can be fruitfully employed in the context of distributed optimization over time-varing networks.
